author: Associated Press
description:
Slinger Francisco, who performed as the Mighty Sparrow, died on Sunday surrounded by family in New York

Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.

Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: Mighty Sparrow, the Trinidad and Tobago singer known as the ‘calypso king of the world’, dies aged 91

author: Associated Press
description:
Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists

Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.

Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19kph). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph (165kph).

Continue reading...
title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico's Baja braces for major Hurricane Polo

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians along the east coast are reporting many sightings of endangered bogong moths as the insects continue their long migration towards the country’s alpine regions.

Bogong moths, about the size of a bottle cap with a distinctive dark stripe that runs down each wing behind two white spots, used to be incredibly abundant. But populations collapsed by up to 99.5% in the two years before 2019.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: Chalmers and Gallagher to present final budget outcome; RBA interest rate hike looms

author: Edward Helmore
description:
US attorney general argues that president is ‘sick and tired’ of inaccurate reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico

Donald Trump’s attorney general Todd Blanche argued on Sunday that the administration banned three news outlets from the White House because it is “privilege … not a right” to be there.

Appearing on the ABC News program This Week during the second week of the White House’s dispute over press credentialing and access, Blanche also said that the administration took the decision to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico beginning on 19 September because the president was “sick and tired” of what he considered to be those media outlets’ inaccurate reporting.

Continue reading...
title: Blanche defends Trump’s White House media ban: ‘It’s a privilege … not a right’

author: Achol Arok
description:
Exclusive: Dedicated service to support sexual assault victim-survivors as they navigate legal system to open in NSW

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

It took Shannon Stokes two years and 11 days to successfully prosecute her former boyfriend for sexual assault and domestic violence offences. The lengthy trial left her feeling as though “there wasn’t going to be an end in sight”.

Prosecutors secured convictions on nine of the 11 charges, and he was later sentenced to five years in prison.

Continue reading...
title: Shannon felt a ‘sense of doom’ as she sought justice for sexual assault. A new NSW program hopes to alleviate that

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Thom Tillis says Trump’s decision to back Paxton over John Cornyn has put the Senate seat at risk for Republicans

US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump, his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary.

“He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary.

Continue reading...
title: Republican says Trump’s support of Ken Paxton in Texas primary was ‘colossal mistake’

author: Jessica Elgot and Rajeev Syal
description:
Exclusive: Move by Shabana Mahmood comes after closure of Afghan scheme last year but experts say numbers too small to deter Channel crossings

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Shabana Mahmood will announce a new legal route for refugees that prioritises Afghan women and girls and Palestinians, unfreezing a scheme that will put the most vulnerable refugees on a faster path to permanent status.

The change marks a shift in Mahmood’s approach to asylum seekers after the abrupt closure of the Afghan resettlement scheme last year and changes that will keep refugee status under constant review for two decades.

Continue reading...
title: UK to open new refugee resettlement routes for Afghan women and Palestinians

author: Shane Harrison
description:
Governments will be hoping row over the contentious Orange Order march down Garvaghy Road can be defused

  • Portadown march: latest updates

Like a ghost from its troubled past, Drumcree has unexpectedly reappeared to remind people how far Northern Ireland has changed in 30 years but also how easily history can undermine the present, if imperfect, peace and stability.

Three decades ago parts of Northern Ireland came to an almost annual standstill as Protestant Orange Order protesters blocked roads in support of members wanting to march down what they called its traditional route, the Garvaghy Road, on the Sunday before the annual 12 July parade.

Continue read
title: Drumcree standoff shows Northern Ireland’s troubled past still threatens its peace

author: Sarah Butler and Alexandra Topping
description:
Airport chiefs say 2035 operations deadline unachievable as critics say new delay makes case for project ‘even more dubious’

Plans for a third runway at Heathrow are once again up in the air after the prime minister refused to say whether he backs the “contested” project which is delayed by up to four years.

Over the weekend it emerged that ​Heathrow no longer expects to meet the original 2035 deadline. Instead, the airport hopes to secure planning permission by 2029 and then open the runway “within a decade”, meaning it would not be operational until 2039.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham dodges questions on Heathrow third runway as project faces four-year delay

author: Sarah Martin
description:
Exclusive: Documents seen by Guardian Australia show that Kelvin Morton has also clashed with party HQ staff and Brisbane volunteers

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation’s general manager, Kelvin Morton – brought in by the party to improve its vetting processes – referred to David Farley as an “asshole” just days before Farley’s historic Farrer byelection win for the party in May.

In a series of text messages seen by Guardian Australia, Morton responds to a
title: One Nation boss called David Farley an ‘asshole’ in lead-up to Farrer byelection, text messages reveal

author: Dan Milmo
description:
‘People care about the songs, books and pictures that influence the critical moments in their lives,’ says the architect of the fightback in the UK

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

If you want to state the case against copyright reform in Australia, get Kylie Minogue’s phone number.

If there is one lesson to be learned from a similar battle in the UK, high-profile members of the creative industries make a difference. They get your argument on the front of newspapers, in the news bulletins and on social media.

Continue reading...
title: British celebrities beat AI companies lobbying to get free use of their work. They have a warning for Australia

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Outcome of meetings of Reserve Bank on Monday and Tuesday will affect Australian mortgage rates, household budgets and house prices

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s key interest rate is expected to hit its highest level since 2011, drag down house prices and add more than $100 to typical monthly mortgage repayments.

The Reserve Bank board is poised to hike the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6% on Tuesday, which would be the fourth increase in 2026 and push typical home loan interest rates to 6.5%.

Continue reading...
title: RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Firms manipulating process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental groups warn

Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental advocates allege.

Companies need federal permits to emit a range of pollutants. In their permit applications, some in big tech are avoiding “major” reviews by dividing their emissions sources into separate, multiple “minor” sources that require less regulatory oversight, the advocates say.

Continue reading...
title: Datacenter developers accused of skirting key US pollution rules

author: Jamie Grierson and Helena Horton
description:
Local people say members of WhatsApp group noticed suspicious activity around vans in Whelford overnight

Those living near RAF Fairford have been used to disturbance from protesters and a heavy police presence after the decision to allow the US air force to use it as a base for attacks on Iran.

But in recent weeks, people have noticed dramatically increased security measures, with the gates of the base newly barricaded.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Police were banging on the door’: villagers near RAF Fairford describe evacuation

author: Associated Press
description:
Pandas departed Chengdu for their new homes in Georgia as part of agreement between Chinese and US governments

Two giant pandas departed Chengdu in south-western China early on Sunday for their new homes in Atlanta, Georgia, as part of an agreement between the Chinese and US governments.

While in Washington DC for a three-day summit with Donald Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping annou
title: Two giant pandas set off to Atlanta zoo from China after Xi-Trump summit

author: Helena Horton
description:
Presenter reveals corporation has been paying part of their salaries to keep his Herefordshire garden camera-ready

For 15 years, viewers have looked in amazement at Monty Don’s beautiful Herefordshire garden, known as Longmeadow, as he hosted the show Gardeners’ World from his own back yard.

But now the BBC presenter, who announced earlier this month that he was leaving the show, has said he may have to let go of the gardeners who have kept the space beautiful and broadcast-ready.

Continue reading...
title: Monty Don says he may have to let go of his gardeners after leaving BBC

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Various factors block sufferers of disease from receiving treatment that is effective and has widespread availability

Sickle cell patients are missing out on an effective treatment despite widespread US hospital access to the technology, new research has found.

That treatment is called a red blood cell exchange, a procedure that discards a patient’s damaged red blood cells while simultaneously mixing the patient’s remaining plasma, platelets and white blood cells with red blood cells from a donor before returning them to the body.

Continue reading...
title: Only 3% of US sickle cell patients receive red blood cell exchange for disease, researchers find

author: Amelia Hill
description:
Decision to allow development of 190 new homes in north Somerset sparks campaign for change in the law

Houses can be built on floodplains even if they fail a crucial safety test, according to a high court judgment that will be of “immense interest” to developers across England and Wales.

The ruling clears the way for a highly controversial development of 190 new homes on north Somerset’s floodplains, despite the site being in “flood zone 3a”, the highest level of flood risk before land is considered a functional floodplain.

Continue reading...
title: Houses can be built on floodplains despite failing safety test, says high court

author: Peter Beaumont and Artem Mazhulin
description:
Supplies cut off from Ukrainian city where bodies are being left to be eaten by dogs because of deadly risk from drones

The phone message sent out of Russian-occupied Oleshky was grimly matter of fact: food for the 2,000 or so civilians still remaining in the city and its surrounding villages had finally run out.

“We’re in Oleshky [and] we can’t get out. We’re going hungry … Right now, I’ve got absolutely nothing to eat,” read the message, from a woman in the besieged city, who was waiting to be evacuated by the occupying forces.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Hell on earth’: last residents eat weeds to survive in Russian-occupied Oleshky

author: Eduardo Porter
description:
‘The push against datacenters speaks to the frustration of people who don’t feel they are making the choices in their lives’

The Stanford ethicist Rob Reich was once invited to a dinner organized by a Silicon Valley mogul to discuss what a state designed to maximize science and tech powered by commercial models might look like. The gathered technologists were drawn to the idea of building a small nation-state dedicated to the endeavor, Reich recalls in “System Error: Where Big Tech Went Wrong and How We Can Reboot it”.

When Reich asked whether this state would be a democracy, he got a cool no. “Democracy is too slow, and it holds science back,” he was told. “To optimize for science, we need a beneficent technocrat in charge.”

Continue reading...
title: Democracy blindsides Silicon Valley’s power players looking to transform the world with AI

author: Gloria Dickie
description:
Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer

Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.

Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found
title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys

author: Helena Horton
description:
People evacuated from village as army inspects vehicles near airbase in Gloucestershire used by US forces

Several men have been arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act after the declaration of a major incident at RAF Fairford.

Homes were evacuated and the army was also inspecting a number of vehicles as security was stepped up at the Gloucestershire airbase, which is used by US forces. Evacuated residents were being taken to a nearby leisure centre.

Continue reading...
title: Major incident declared near RAF Fairford as men held on suspicion of explosives offences

author: Associated Press in Cape Town
description:
Seventeen people killed at township bar near Johannesburg and 10 killed in separate incident at store near Cape Town, officers say

Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, police have said.

The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, south-west of Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

Continue reading...
title: At least 27 dead in two mass shootings in South Africa, police say

author: Lauren Cochrane
description:
A look evoking memories of All Saints and Destiny’s Child has fashion editors, Brad Pitt and the high street all blending in

Discussing their style while in All Saints, Nicole and Natalie Appleton said earlier this year that some things don’t change: “Army trousers and combat trousers will always be a staple with us.”

If, for a long time after All Saints’ noughties heyday, the sisters would have known this look was not the height of fashion, things have changed in 2026. Judging by those attending shows at London fashion week this month, camo is very much back.

Continue reading...
title: Camo’s back: noughties pop’s military style is on the march again

author: Helena Horton
description:
Unauthorised people accessed medical records of three-year-old who disappeared in Suffolk and was later found dead in pond

An NHS trust has apologised after the medical records of three-year-old Noah Woods were accessed by unauthorised people after his disappearance.

Noah was found dead in a pond in Brantham, Suffolk, after going missing from a playground. More than 1,300 members of the public joined a search for the boy before police discovered his body.

Continue reading...
title: NHS trust apologises as 10 staff suspended over Noah Woods data breach

author: Associated Press
description:
Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected ways

OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.

The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.

Continue reading...
title: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Many applicants left feeling ‘used, lied to, misled and gaslit’, complaint letter seen by Guardian Australia says

  • Listen to the Guardian podcast The Populist here

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation could collect as much as $633,000 from people who have put their hand up to run in the Victorian state election, with potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.

Guardian Australia has spoken to
title: ‘Cash grab’: One Nation demands up to $630,000 from Victorian election candidates

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow live updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Partner of NSW police officer who died in crash says he’s lost the love of his life

Daniel Vasquez, the partner of NSW police officer Mia Lay, who died in a car crash while on duty, issued a statement on behalf of her family yesterday, saying he had lost the “love of my life”.

Mia loved what she did in the police. She was happy in the police, she was good at her job, and how loved she was by everyone in the community. She was the happiest girl I’ve met …

I’d ask for everyone to remember how stunning and beautiful she was. She was a kind hearted person, gave so much love to everyone that she cared about …
title: Australia news live: Marles said OpenAI CEO didn’t tell him about hack at meeting; flight cancellation heartbreak for AFL fans
